text:
julia_support: FYI customer reported intermittent 401s after rotating API key. Only affects their long-lived worker fleet (async socketpool + uvicorn/gunicorn) — restart clears it. Repro steps below. SUP-8742.
ryan_eng: thanks, can you paste minimal repro? is this using module-level client or per-request creation?
julia_support: they init client at module import in background task: `client = RedwoodClient()` then worker threads reuse it. After vault rotation they update env and k8s secret, pods don't restart. 401s start ~2-10m after rotation.
alex_dev: sounds like stale headers being kept on pooled connections. requests/urllib3 keepalive will reuse TCP connection with old authorization header baked into session-level headers if client was created with header at init.
mai_sre: also check if gunicorn `preload_app True` is set — that will create client in master then fork, causing children to share socket state unexpectedly.
ryan_eng: request: please include SDK version. Some older py-sdk versions cached the org header in a private session and didn't expose a `set_api_key` API.
julia_support: sdk_version: 2.0.3, python: 3.10. Customer tested upgrading to 2.2.1 and issue reduced but still occasional 401s.
samir: quick repro I used:```# app.py
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ.get('REDWOOD_KEY'))
async def background_job():
    while True:
        await client.generate("hi")
        await asyncio.sleep(1)
```
Start, rotate env var in pod (not restarting process) -> subsequent calls 401.
alex_dev: root cause: connection pool reuses sockets; server-side auth might be validated per-TLS session and token rotation means new token invalid relative to connection context. Also session.headers may still reference old token. Closing pool forces new connections with updated headers.
mai_sre: workaround: either recreate client after rotation or call `client._session.close()` (not ideal public API) or set per-request header: `client.generate(..., headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {new_key}"})`.
ryan_eng: for customers running with Vault -> recommend a small shim: on secret update event, call a health endpoint that triggers a graceful restart or send SIGHUP to worker to reload secrets and `client = RedwoodClient(...)` again.
julia_support: customer said they can't restart pods for compliance reasons. Any hot-rotate best practice?
samir: options: 1) SDK change to support `client.update_api_key(new)` that also recreates internal session/pool. 2) Use short-lived per-request client creation (costly). 3) Use connection header `"Connection": "close"` to avoid pooling (adds latency). 4) patch requests pool by calling `session.close()` after set.
alex_dev: added note: uvicorn with `--reload` or dev setups differ. Production: gunicorn with workers + preload is common pitfall. If preload_app=True, recreate clients in post_fork hook.
mai_sre: quick command to clear pools without restart: `from requests import sessions; sessions.Session().close()` not enough; you need to close the actual session held by SDK instance. If they can't call internal API, set `env REDWOOD_API_KEY` on a sidecar that proxies and injects header per-request.
ryan_eng: can you ask customer to test this quick probe and paste logs? `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $NEW" http://127.0.0.1:8000/_probe` and then run one request via SDK — check if 401 persists.
samir: filing internal follow-up: engineering should add public `client.update_api_key` + `client._recreate_session()` in next minor release and doc snippet on hot-rotate.
deploy-bot: deploy noted: created branch fix/hot-rotate-sdk (CI queued). :rocket:
julia_support: customer accepted workaround to add sidecar proxy for header injection and will test. Closing provisional until more data. Thanks all :thumbsup:
